learningObjectives: Explain the role of a TestSheet within the TestCase Design section.
Create and structure Attributes to represent the business objects and behaviors under test.
Distinguish the system-assigned AttrType (Logical vs Physical) from the user-assigned BusinessRelevant property.
Apply the four recommended core Attributes: Administration, Precondition, Process, and Verification.

elements.description: The highest-level object in the TestCase Design section. A TestSheet organizes the test data and logical test structure for one Requirement — as a rule of thumb, one TestSheet is created per Requirement, and the TestCases built from it will cover that Requirement.

A characteristic or business object involved in the behavior being tested — for example, a credit-card drop-down on a checkout form. Attributes describe *what varies*; the specific values an Attribute can take (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) are added later as Instances (Lesson 3).
Like Requirements, Attributes can be layered — every Attribute may have sub-Attributes, depending on how much detail the TestSheet needs.

bulletPoints: One TestSheet per Requirement is the standard rule of thumb.
Attribute = the characteristic; Instance (next lesson) = the specific value of that characteristic.

elements.description: Every Attribute has an AttrType property with value 'Logical' or 'Physical'. This isn't something you choose from a dropdown — Tosca sets it automatically based on structure: an Attribute with sub-Attributes underneath it is Logical; an Attribute with none is Physical.

bulletPoints: Logical = has sub-Attributes. Physical = does not. Tosca decides this for you based on structure.

elements.description: Tricentis recommends starting every TestSheet with four top-level logical Attributes, so that any reader can immediately see the role each block of data plays.

elements.title: Administration / Precondition / Process / Verification
items: Administration — metadata about the TestCase itself (designer, contact person, test stage, comments). Not actual test data, and not business relevant.
Precondition — prerequisite data needed to get the application/workspace into the right starting state (e.g. login credentials). Required to run, but not the focus of the test.
Process — the actual data being tested; directly relevant to the TestCase's purpose.
Verification — data used to check whether the process behaved as expected; comparison/expected-result values.

bulletPoints: Administration = context, not test data. Precondition = setup. Process = what's under test. Verification = expected outcome.

elements.description: BusinessRelevant is set by the user (unlike AttrType) and controls whether an Attribute's data affects TestCase combinations.

elements.title: Yes / No / Result
items: Yes (default) — the Attribute is business relevant and should be considered when combining data into TestCases. Typical for Precondition and Process.
No — the Attribute (and its sub-Attributes) is not relevant to combinations. Typical for Administration.
Result — the Attribute (and its sub-Attributes) holds verification data used for comparisons. Typical for Verification.

elements.text: Setting BusinessRelevant on a parent Attribute propagates that value down to all of its sub-Attributes.

bulletPoints: Map the four core Attributes to BusinessRelevant like this: Administration=No, Precondition=Yes, Process=Yes, Verification=Result.

elements.title: Creating a TestSheet (3 ways)
items: Right-click a Folder → 'Create TestSheet' from the Mini-Toolbar

elements.text: BusinessRelevant is set on the Attribute's Properties tab (Yes/No/Result dropdown), or toggled with Ctrl+F7 or the corresponding Ribbon button. The Attribute's color changes in the tree to reflect its current value.

📄 Exercise 02a-02b (TestSheet and Basic Attribute Structure, Attribute Structure — Process and Verification) — Official Tricentis Academy course material, not redistributed here. Access it inside the official course.

bulletPoints: Best practice: mirror the Requirements Folder structure in the TestCase Design section (not always followed in training workspaces for simplicity).

examPitfalls.title: Trying to manually set AttrType
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Looking for a dropdown or button to set an Attribute's AttrType to Logical or Physical.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: AttrType is calculated automatically by Tosca based on structure — Logical if the Attribute has sub-Attributes, Physical if it does not. It is not user-editable.

examPitfalls.title: Leaving Administration as BusinessRelevant = Yes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Forgetting to set the Administration Attribute's business relevance, so metadata like 'Test Designer' gets pulled into combinatorics.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Administration should be set to BusinessRelevant = No, since it holds context/metadata, not data that should influence which combinations are generated.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing Precondition and Process
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Placing the actual data under test inside Precondition, or setup/login data inside Process.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Precondition holds prerequisite setup data (not the test's focus, e.g. login info); Process holds the data that is actually the focus of the TestCase.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming BusinessRelevant settings apply per-Attribute only
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Manually re-setting BusinessRelevant on every sub-Attribute after already setting it on the parent.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: BusinessRelevant set on a parent Attribute automatically propagates to all of its sub-Attributes — no need to repeat it lower in the tree.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An Attribute called 'Credit Card' contains sub-Attributes for card number, expiry date, and card type. What AttrType will Tosca assign to 'Credit Card'?

options.text: Physical, because it represents a physical payment card.
The user must choose manually via a dropdown.
AttrType only applies to Instances, not Attributes.

practiceQuiz.hint: AttrType is derived from structure, not chosen by the user.
practiceQuiz.rationale: AttrType is set automatically by Tosca: an Attribute with sub-Attributes is Logical; one without is Physical. It cannot be manually assigned.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which BusinessRelevant value should the Verification Attribute typically use?
practiceQuiz.hint: This value flags an Attribute as holding comparison/expected-outcome data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Verification is typically set to BusinessRelevant = Result, indicating it holds data used for verifications/comparisons rather than data that should drive combinatorics.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester sets the top-level Administration Attribute's BusinessRelevant to 'No'. What happens to its sub-Attributes (e.g. 'Test Designer', 'Comments')?

options.text: Nothing — each sub-Attribute must be set individually.
They automatically inherit BusinessRelevant = No from the parent.
They automatically switch to AttrType = Physical.

practiceQuiz.hint: BusinessRelevant is a property that flows down the tree.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Setting BusinessRelevant on a parent Attribute propagates that setting to all of its sub-Attributes automatically.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which shortcut creates a new Attribute directly (without using the Ribbon or right-click menu)?
practiceQuiz.hint: T is for TestSheet, R is for Requirement — this one is for the object covered in this lesson.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Ctrl+N, Ctrl+A creates an Attribute. Ctrl+N, Ctrl+T creates a TestSheet, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+R creates a Requirement, and Ctrl+F7 toggles BusinessRelevant on a selected Attribute.

quickRecap.value: Top-level TestCase Design object; one per Requirement, as a rule of thumb.
A characteristic/business object; can have sub-Attributes.
System-assigned: Logical (has sub-Attributes) or Physical (does not). Not user-editable.
Yes / No / Result — user-set, propagates to sub-Attributes, controls inclusion in combinatorics.
